SMTO-CFG-0009 — The Gateway couldn't start: idle terminal time limit is too low

GUID: 3e735107-2e60-4265-810d-e1f31592940f
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-terminal-idle-timeout-seconds-must-be
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, stopped right after starting. Its limit for how long an unused terminal may stay open is set to zero or less, which isn't allowed. No settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, find GATEWAY_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in the command or settings used to start it. This setting holds the value the Gateway refused.
  2. Set it to a number of seconds above zero, such as 3600 (one hour, the normal value), or remove it so the Gateway uses that normal value. The Gateway closes terminals left unused for this long, so it needs a real amount of time.
  3. Start the Gateway again. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. This shows whether the Gateway now starts with the corrected value and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway keeps running after it starts, and in Settings › Setup › Gateways it shows Connected.

If it still fails

  • Copy the error shown where the Gateway was started (or select Copy error details if SMTO shows it) and send it to the person who set up this Gateway. Don't use 0 to mean "never close"; this setting doesn't allow it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway settings validation rejected terminal_idle_timeout_seconds (GATEWAY_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) because it is zero or negative; it must be greater than zero.

What this means

  • terminal_idle_timeout_seconds is zero or negative during Gateway configuration validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • terminal_idle_timeout_seconds is zero or negative during Gateway configuration validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS separately from command execution deadlines.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS on the Gateway host to a positive number of seconds (default 3600; workspace terminals still enforce at least 60) or unset it to use the default, then restart the Gateway.
  • Set GATEWAY_TERMINAL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to a positive duration on the Gateway host.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended positive terminal-idle duration passes startup validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
